reference.source: Firestein & Kelley's Textbook of Rheumatology / Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine
clinicalPearls: A rare non-Langerhans histiocytosis, now recognised as a clonal myeloid neoplasm, usually presenting in middle-aged and older adults
Bilateral symmetrical osteosclerosis of the long bones (particularly around the knees) with bone pain is the most consistent finding
Perirenal infiltration produces the characteristic 'hairy kidney' appearance and periaortic encasement the 'coated aorta' on cross-sectional imaging
Central nervous system, retro-orbital, cardiac (periaortic and right atrial pseudotumour), and pituitary involvement (diabetes insipidus) are common and drive morbidity
A large majority carry activating BRAF-V600E or other MAPK pathway mutations, which are both diagnostic and therapeutic targets
Histology shows foamy (lipid-laden) CD68-positive, CD1a-negative histiocytes with Touton giant cells and surrounding fibrosis
Targeted BRAF and MEK inhibition has transformed treatment of mutation-positive disease; interferon has historically been used
reference.pathophysiology: Erdheim-Chester disease is a clonal histiocytic neoplasm arising from myeloid precursors, driven in most cases by activating mutations of the MAPK/ERK signalling pathway, most commonly BRAF-V600E. Constitutive pathway activation leads to accumulation and tissue infiltration by foamy, lipid-laden non-Langerhans histiocytes accompanied by fibrosis and an inflammatory milieu. This produces the characteristic bilateral long-bone osteosclerosis, perirenal and periaortic sheathing, and infiltration of the central nervous system, orbit, heart, and hypothalamic-pituitary axis, the last causing diabetes insipidus.
additionalInvestigations: Biopsy of an affected site showing foamy CD68-positive, CD1a-negative histiocytes with Touton giant cells
Molecular testing for BRAF-V600E and other MAPK pathway mutations
Plain radiographs and technetium bone scan showing symmetrical long-bone osteosclerosis
CT of chest, abdomen, and pelvis for perirenal 'hairy kidney' and periaortic 'coated aorta'
MRI of brain and cardiac imaging to assess neurological and cardiac infiltration
PET imaging to map disease extent and monitor treatment response
redFlags: Cardiac infiltration or pericardial involvement threatening haemodynamic compromise
Central nervous system involvement with neurological deterioration
Diabetes insipidus and other hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction
Renal impairment from perirenal and periureteric encasement
reference.prognosis: Prognosis depends on the extent and site of involvement; central nervous system and cardiac disease historically carried high mortality, but targeted BRAF/MEK inhibition has markedly improved outcomes in mutation-positive patients.
pitfalls: Mistaking foamy histiocytes for Langerhans cell histiocytosis without immunostaining (CD1a) and molecular testing
Attributing bone pain to degenerative disease and missing the symmetrical osteosclerosis
Overlooking cardiac and central nervous system involvement that determine prognosis
Failing to test for BRAF-V600E, which guides targeted therapy
Confusing periaortic and perirenal disease with retroperitoneal fibrosis alone
management: Targeted therapy with a BRAF inhibitor (vemurafenib or dabrafenib) for BRAF-V600E-mutant disease, the principal disease-modifying treatment
MEK inhibition (cobimetinib or trametinib) for non-BRAF MAPK-pathway-mutant or BRAF-inhibitor-intolerant disease
Interferon-alpha as an alternative systemic option, particularly where targeted agents are unavailable
Hormone replacement for hypothalamic-pituitary infiltration, including desmopressin for cranial diabetes insipidus and replacement of other deficient pituitary hormones
Analgesia and supportive care for long-bone pain, with orthopaedic input for symptomatic osteosclerotic disease
Cardiac and neurological monitoring for periaortic, right-atrial pseudotumour and central nervous system infiltration, which drive morbidity
Serial PET imaging to map disease extent and monitor response to targeted therapy
Coordinated multidisciplinary care across haematology, cardiology, endocrinology and neurology
